pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does fluent reading mean? (1 mark)
   A. Skipping words
   B. Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   C. Reading in a whisper
   D. Reading very slowly word by word

2. Which question helps you find ideas from a picture? (1 mark)
   A. Who is in the picture?
   B. What page is this?
   C. Who printed it?
   D. How heavy is the paper?

3. What does interpret mean? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To explain what something means
   C. To tear it
   D. To sell it

4. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. Money left after paying the cost
   B. A kind of shop
   C. Money spent
   D. A bill

5. What should you do while a classmate recites? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Listen and respect them
   C. Leave
   D. Talk

6. What does turn taking mean? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking all at once
   B. Refusing to speak
   C. Speaking loudest
   D. Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance

7. Which of these is a preposition? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. banana
   C. behind
   D. jump

8. What are notes? (1 mark)
   A. Long stories
   B. Short records of important points
   C. Pictures only
   D. Songs

9. What does Many hands make light work mean? (1 mark)
   A. Work is always easy
   B. Nobody should help
   C. Hands are light
   D. Work is easier when people share it

10. What should you keep the same in a paragraph unless there is a reason to change? (1 mark)
   A. The paper colour
   B. The pen
   C. The time of the verbs
   D. The page

11. What should a reader do at a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. Pause briefly
   B. Shout
   C. Skip a line
   D. Turn the page

12. What is a gallery walk in handwriting practice? (1 mark)
   A. A race in the field
   B. A song
   C. A test of running
   D. Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display

13. Which of these is a cultural food word? (1 mark)
   A. pencil
   B. ruler
   C. window
   D. porridge

14. How should you start a new speaker's words in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. At the end of the page
   B. On the same line as before
   C. Inside a bracket
   D. On a new line

15. Which word shows the first step? (1 mark)
   A. In the end
   B. Finally
   C. First
   D. Lastly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Give three qualities of a good leader mentioned in the model poem lead with honesty. (3 marks)

17. Explain why leaders are important and why people should obey fair leaders. Give two examples of leaders in a community. (5 marks)

18. List three steps for explaining a proverb. (3 marks)

19. Explain what turn taking means. (2 marks)

20. Explain what an oral narrative is. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   Fluent readers read smoothly.

2. A — Who is in the picture?
   Who, where, what and why give story ideas.

3. B — To explain what something means
   To interpret is to explain meaning.

4. A — Money left after paying the cost
   Profit is gain after costs.

5. B — Listen and respect them
   Good listeners respect performers.

6. D — Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance
   Turn taking is orderly speaking.

7. C — behind
   Behind shows position.

8. B — Short records of important points
   Notes are brief points.

9. D — Work is easier when people share it
   It is a proverb about working together.

10. C — The time of the verbs
   Keep past, present or future consistent.

11. A — Pause briefly
   Full stops tell us to pause.

12. D — Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display
   Pupils view and comment on displayed work.

13. D — porridge
   Porridge is a food. The others are not.

14. D — On a new line
   A new line shows a new speaker.

15. C — First
   First begins the sequence.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fair, true, listens, shares the work, kind, strong (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: Leaders guide, make decisions and keep order. Obeying fair leaders keeps peace and safety. Examples: chief, teacher, class monitor, elders.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for why leaders are important, two marks for obeying and one for examples.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say it slowly, picture what it shows, decide the lesson, think of a real situation, explain in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means speaking one person at a time and waiting for others to finish before speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for one at a time and one for waiting.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: An oral narrative is a story told aloud, passed on from person to person, that entertains and teaches.
   Working / marking points: One mark for told aloud and one mark for entertain or teach.
